concepts.title: Factors of Natural Numbers and Algebraic Expressions
concepts.definition: Every natural number breaks into a product of primes, and every algebraic expression breaks into a product of its irreducible factors - factorisation writes a quantity as a multiplication instead of a sum.
concepts.key_idea: Factorisation is division in reverse: find what multiplies to the given expression.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh112.txt sections 12.1.1-12.2 (factors of natural numbers, what is factorisation)
question_patterns: write the given number as a product of primes
what are the factors of the given expression
define factorisation with an example
find the irreducible factors of the given term
determine whether the given factorisation is complete
express the monomial as a product of irreducible factors

solution_steps.explain: Break numerals into primes and letters into powers.
Stop when every factor is prime or a bare variable power.
Multiplying the factors must rebuild the original.

concepts.title: Factorisation by Common Factors and Regrouping
concepts.definition: Two workhorse methods open factorisation: pull out the greatest common factor from every term, and regroup terms so each new group shares a factor - as 2xy + 2y + 3x + 3 regroups into (x + 1)(2y + 3).
concepts.key_idea: Take out what is common, then arrange what remains into matching groups.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh112.txt sections 12.2.1-12.2.2 (method of common factors, regrouping)
question_patterns: factorise the given expression by taking out the common factor
factorise 6xy - 4y by the common factor method
factorise the expression by regrouping the terms
factorise 2xy + 2y + 3x + 3
what is the greatest common factor of the given terms
check the factorisation by multiplying back

solution_steps.explain: Take the HCF of coefficients and the common letters.
The expression becomes the common factor times the remaining sum.
Pair the terms so each group offers a shared bracket.

concepts.title: Factorisation Using Identities
concepts.definition: Standard identities run backwards into factorisation: a squared plus 2ab plus b squared is (a + b) squared, a squared minus 2ab plus b squared is (a - b) squared, and a squared minus b squared factors as (a + b)(a - b).
concepts.key_idea: Recognise the pattern, name a and b, and the factors appear as a bracket pair.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh112.txt sections 12.2.3-12.2.4 (factorisation using identities, factors of the given form)
question_patterns: factorise x squared + 8x + 16 using identities
factorise 49a squared - 36b squared
use the identity to factorise the given expression
factorise the perfect square trinomial
express the difference of squares as a product
factorise m squared - 4n squared and verify

solution_steps.explain: Compare the expression with the three standard identity forms.
The squared terms reveal the a and b of the identity.
The identity's right side gives the bracket pair directly.

concepts.title: Division of Algebraic Expressions
concepts.definition: Division undoes factorisation: dividing a monomial by a monomial cancels common factors between coefficients and letters, and dividing a polynomial by a monomial splits it term by term, as 8x squared by 2x leaves 4x.
concepts.key_idea: Cancel common factors top and bottom - coefficients divide, powers subtract.
question_patterns: divide 8x squared by 2x
divide the given polynomial by the monomial
simplify the division of the given monomials
divide 24x cubed y by 6xy and verify
perform the division and check by multiplying back
find the quotient of the given algebraic division

solution_steps.explain: The numeric parts cancel by common factors.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Divide the monomial {coef1}x by {coef2}x. What is the numerical coefficient of the quotient?
In the division of the monomials with coefficients {coef1} and {coef2}, find the quotient's coefficient.

solution_template.explain: The quotient coefficient is the ratio.
